newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: BELGRADE BOURSE TURNOVER DOWN IN WEEK TO AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: BELGRADE BOURSE TURNOVER DOWN IN WEEK TO AUG 8.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 15 percent decline in turnover dragging its short-term debentures index 71.18 points down in the week to August 8.
Market activity was subdued due to holiday season with many market participants away until the end of August, traders said.
Total turnover dropped to 101.9 million dinars ($16.06 million) in 102 transactions from 116.89 million dinars in 136 deals a week ago.
The BSE index of short-term debentures fell to 214.73 index points from 285.91 points a week ago.
Liquidity of the banking sector was good with their average sight deposits totalling 2.8 billion dinars. But bank lending activity was insignificant, traders said.
Some analysts saw banks refraining from substantial credit operations ahead of August 15, when most of them financing the farm sector will have to pay farmers for the 1997 crop.
"All those deposits will soon be spent to pay out farmers. This year there will be no bargaining with farmers as they constitute an important electorate," a trader told Reuters.
Others said interest rates ranging between a monthly 5.5 and 6.5 percent were not high enough to compensate risky loans.
Some traders believed overall economic and financial activity will remain low until after the September 21 presidential and parliamentary elections in Serbia.
For the week ending August 8, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 87 deals totalling 23.343 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded six times for a total of 0.84 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between a monthly 5.00 and 10.00 percent while maturity stood between seven and 360 days.
* The bourse reported two deals in state T-bills worth 1.8 million dinars.
* There were five transactions in the central-bank short-term bonds totalling 72.5 million dinars.
The central bank expanded last week its previous 50 million dinar tranche of bonds with another 50 million dinars, keeping the rate on bonds unchanged at an annual 43.63 percent.
* OTC trade in commercial paper and treasury bills fell to 57.23 million dinars from 100.32 million a week ago.

* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, inched up to 26.75 million dinars from 26.6 million a week ago. NOTE -- The BSE short-term debentures index is calculated on volume, interest rate and maturity of the most frequently bourse-traded short-term commercial paper and treasury bills. Index base is 1996. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
